traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Rousseaceae: leaves usually alternate, rarely opposite; leaves simple; margins dentate or serrate; veins pinnate; leaves evergreen; blades ovate or lanceolate; stipules absent; plants hermaphrodite or polygamous; ovary usually superior, rarely half inferior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers solitary, in panicles or in corymbs; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule or berry; parts of each whorl 5 (-6); stamens 5 (-6); carpels 5 (-7). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
